ENFORCEMENT ACTIONS
October 202 3
DOB ISSUES MONTHLY ENFORCEMENT BULLETIN
Report Highlights DOB Enforcement Outcomes from October 2023 to Deter
Bad Actors and Keep New Yorkers Safe
New York, NY – Today, the New York City Department of Buildings released its
enforcement bulletin for October 2023, which provides highlights of the agency’s actions
to sanction and deter bad actors in the construction industry through the enforcement of
safety laws and codes of conduct. Today’s bulletin includes summaries of DOB-
imposed disciplinary actions, including penalties, license suspensions and revocations.
The actions below represent a portion of DOB’s overall work to enforce the City’s
building codes and safety laws, in addition to the thousands of inspections conducted
and violations issued by the agency each month for illegal building and construction
conditions.
DOB completed a number of major enforcement actions in October, including:
• 18 violations and $210,000 in penalties issued for failure to safeguard
construction sites on 18 separate occasions.
• 11 violations and $178,750 in penalties, including daily penalties, issued for
illegal building alterations at 2 locations.
• 3 violations and $30,000 in penalties issued to 3 individuals for failure to carry out
the duties of a construction superintendent.
Below are individual enforcement highlights for October 2023:
Bronx
• $10,000 in penalties issued to Skanska RJ Industries for violations recorded at
221 Miranda Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard
after an excavator hit overhead powerline, breaking two electric poles and
damaging Con Ed powerlines.
• $2,500 in penalties issued to Quad Stars LLC for violations at 387 Fordham
Road. DOB inspectors found the respondent had failed to register a sign into the
sign inventory for their Outdoor Advertising Company.

Brooklyn
• $124,000 in total penalties issued to Abul Khair for violations recorded at 183
Minna Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for illegal alterations about
finding 3 additional dwellings added, including 4 SROs in the cellar.
• $54,250 in total penalties issued to Mohammed J Akhanji for violations recorded
at 15 Kossuth Place. DOB inspectors issued violations for illegal alteration after
finding 3 additional dwellings with key locks added on third floor.
• $32,500 in total penalties issued to Gilbane Building Company for violations
recorded at 141 Willoughby St. DOB inspectors issued violations after worker
using extension ladder without being tied-off or with three-point stability. fell and
injured hip. Inspectors found no record of pre-shift meeting, or refresher for site
safety orientation.
• $16,000 in total penalties issued to Urban Atelier Group LLC for violations
recorded at 30 Front St. and 60 Front St. DOB inspectors observed no
pedestrian protection available where materials and equipment were being
stored, as well as loose wires throughout, and workers not wearing hard hats.
• $12,500 in total penalties issued to Urban Atelier Group for violations recorded at
267 Bond Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard after a
worker performing stripping operations without guardrails fell 7 feet from
foundation. Additionally, inspectors found insufficient pedestrian protection as
walked was 2 feet wide, not the required width of 5 feet.
• $10,000 in penalties issued to Oliwa Construction for violations recorded at 94
2nd Street. DOB inspectors issued violations after observing 3 workers at a 9-ft-
deep excavation without support or protection, including water seeping in that
was causing foundation to sink.

• $2,500 in penalties issued to Hamoud Construction Corp for violations recorded
at 2129 East 74th Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for work performed on
a Saturday without a required after-hours permit.
• $2,500 in penalties issued to BK Acquisition Three LLC for violations recorded at
180 Remsen Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to maintaion
building after observing front section of building’s finished masonry measuring
4’x4’x2” had detached over a public sidewalk.
• $2,500 in penalties issued to 200-204 Calyer Street LLC for violations recorded
at 200 Calyer Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to maintain
building after finding all fire-stopping removed from ceiling and walls on first floor
of the occupied being, as well as loose electrical wires and open electrical box.
Manhattan
• $35,000 in total penalties issued to Turner Construction Company for violations
recorded at 2 Pen Plaza. DOB inspectors observed workers improperly using
grinder, causing sparks to fly, and worker not using PPE. Additionally, no
guardrails or toe boards were present on scaffold at the location.
• $25,000 in penalties issued to CM and Associates Construction for violations
recorded at 14 5th Avenue. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to
safeguard after inground construction operations caused cracks in an adjacent
building, leading to apartments being vacated.
•
Queens
• $12,500 in total penalties issued to Hunter Roberts Construction for violations
recorded at 26-58 Jackson Ave. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to
institute safety measures after a pile driver being used on muddy ground and
with a defective hoist wire fell on a worker’s leg during operations.
• $7,500 in total penalties issued to 2022 ANJ Construction for violations recorded
at 19-12 149th street. DOB inspectors issued violations for demolition without a
permit and failure to maintain housekeeping.
• $5,000 in total penalties issued to Gavriel Badalov for violations recorded at 147-
07 72nd Drive. DOB inspectors issued violations for work without a permit and
illegal occupancy for electrical work, plumbing, partitions, and a deck at the
second floor.
• DOB inspectors
Staten Island
• $25,000 in penalties issued to Kel-tech Construction Inc for violations recorded at
445 Castleton Ave. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard after
a worker fell off a scaffold that was improperly constructed and material fell on

top of him. Inspectors observed that scaffold had cross braces unsecured, and
levels not fully planked and were missing guardrails.
Construction and Design Professionals
• DOB’s Special Enforcement Team (SET) audited 8 professionally certified
applications submitted by Professional Engineer Solomon Rosenzweig and found
major code non-compliances, including filing Alteration - No CO applications
despite proposing changes in use, egress, and/or occupancy, which require
Alteration - CO applications for a new or amended Certificate of Occupancy;
proposing plans that do properly indicate partial demolition; proposing plans that
show the number of units contrary to the I-card in effect; proposing plans that do
not provide two exits nor stairs equipped with automatic sprinkler protection;
failure to provide complete structural plans; and various other violations of code
and rules, including the Zoning Resolution, Building Code, and Administrative
Code. Based on the audits, SET offered a voluntary surrender of Professional
Certification and Directive 14 privileges, which the Respondent signed.
• DOB’s Special Enforcement Team (SET) audited 8 professionally certified
applications submitted by Registered Architect Dezhang Fang and found major
code non-compliances including filing Alteration - No CO applications despite
proposing changes in use, egress, and/or occupancy, which require Alteration -
CO applications for a new or amended Certificate of Occupancy; proposing plans
that fail to provide two exits from the cellar and fail to show that the cellar stair is
enclosed; proposing plans that improperly include obstructions in the court of a
residential building located in the R7A district; failure to provide a complete
Tenant Protection Plan; and various other violations of code and rules, including
the Zoning Resolution, Building Code, and Administrative Code. Based on the
audits, SET offered a voluntary surrender of Professional Certification and
Directive 14 privileges, which the Respondent signed.
• DOB’s Special Enforcement Team (SET) audited 8 professionally certified
applications submitted by Professional Engineer Sunil Saigal and found major
code non-compliances, including filing Alteration - No CO applications despite
proposing changes in use, egress, and/or occupancy, which require Alteration -
CO applications for a new or amended Certificate of Occupancy; proposing plans
that are incomplete; proposing a cellar staircase that is not entirely enclosed;
failure to correctly identify the required special inspections; and various other
violations of code and rules, including the Zoning Resolution, Building Code, and
Administrative Code. Based on the audits, SET offered a voluntary surrender of
Professional Certification and Directive 14 privileges, which the Respondent
signed.
• General Contractor Sasikanth Simhadri was issued a warning letter reminding
him that all workers working at sites for which he holds city contracts must be
paid prevailing wages. The warning letter was emailed to Simhadri’s attorney.
